profiles.title: The Iveron Icon of the Mother of God
profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Iveron icon is associated with Iviron Monastery on Mount Athos. The OCA explains its Greek title Portaitissa as Gate-Keeper, connecting the name with the icon’s repeated appearance at the monastery’s entrance in the traditional account.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published source; substantial verbatim reproduction is not licensed. This is an editorial summary, not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: The displayed Iveron image shows Mary holding Christ and gesturing toward him, with their faces and hands visible through a decorated metal covering. It is identified by its file source as the Iveron image, not as an unrelated Marian portrait.

blocks.text: The Church narrative begins with a widow near Nicaea during Emperor Theophilos’s iconoclasm. After a soldier wounds the image, she commits it to the sea. The OCA then relates how the Georgian monk Gabriel receives it from the water at Mount Athos. These miraculous events are presented as received Church tradition.

blocks.text: The source associates the icon’s place at the gate with the Mother of God’s protection of the community. Its explanation of the title concerns that particular narrative, while the image itself directs attention to Mary and her Son.
